title: Logical Reasoning
shortDescription: Pattern detection, deduction, sequences and abstract reasoning — measured the way GRE and LSAT logic sections do.
longDescription: Logical Reasoning measures how you detect patterns and draw valid conclusions from stated premises. The assessment has two parts: abstract pattern recognition (shape, color, rotation, quantity and spectrum sequences) and deductive reasoning (syllogisms and conditional logic, including recognizing when a conclusion only might be true rather than must be true).
sourceNote: Ported from airostudio/logical-reasoning (lib/testQuestions.ts). 15 real questions total (6 abstract-pattern, 9 deductive) — short of the catalogue's nominal ~20, not padded with invented ones. The 6 abstract-pattern questions reference real SVG art at public/images/patterns/pattern-{1..6}.svg in the source repo; questionText describes each pattern in words. Porting the actual SVGs as question media is a follow-up.

sections.name: Abstract Pattern Reasoning
sections.description: Visual and numeric pattern-recognition questions where you identify the next item in a sequence based on shape, color, rotation, quantity, or spectrum progression.
sections.instructions: Study each pattern sequence carefully and select the option that correctly continues the pattern.

sections.name: Deductive Reasoning
sections.description: Verbal logic questions testing your ability to draw valid conclusions from given premises, including syllogisms and identification of logical fallacies.
sections.instructions: Read each set of statements carefully and choose the conclusion that logically follows (or correctly identifies that it cannot be determined).

scoringDimensions.label: Logical Reasoning
scoringDimensions.description: Overall composite measure of logical reasoning ability, combining abstract pattern recognition and deductive inference performance.

scoringDimensions.label: Pattern Detection
scoringDimensions.description: Ability to recognize and extrapolate visual and numeric patterns.

scoringDimensions.label: Deductive Inference
scoringDimensions.description: Ability to draw valid conclusions from premises, including recognizing invalid inferences.

resultRanges.title: Developing
resultRanges.description: Basic logical reasoning abilities. Pattern recognition and deductive inference are still forming, with frequent difficulty distinguishing valid conclusions from plausible-sounding but unsupported ones.
recommendations: Practice simple pattern-completion puzzles daily to build sequence recognition
Study the difference between valid syllogisms and common fallacies like affirming the consequent
Work through logic puzzles slowly, writing out each premise before concluding

resultRanges.title: Average
resultRanges.description: Moderate logical reasoning abilities. You can solve straightforward pattern and deduction problems but struggle with multi-step chains or subtler invalid-inference traps.
recommendations: Practice multi-step syllogisms involving three or more premises
Time yourself on pattern sequences to build speed alongside accuracy
Focus on distinguishing 'must be true' from 'might be true' conclusions

resultRanges.title: Strong
resultRanges.description: Good logical reasoning abilities. You solve most pattern-recognition and deductive problems with consistent accuracy, occasionally missing more subtle or multi-layered items.
recommendations: Challenge yourself with abstract reasoning puzzles that combine two changing attributes at once
Practice conditional logic chains (if-then-therefore) with nested conditions
Seek out advanced syllogism sets that include invalid-argument distractors

resultRanges.title: Very Strong
resultRanges.description: Strong logical reasoning abilities. You excel at identifying patterns and drawing valid conclusions, handling most deductive traps and multi-attribute sequences correctly.
recommendations: Tackle competition-style logic puzzles and advanced abstract reasoning sets
Explore formal logic notation to deepen understanding of validity vs. soundness

resultRanges.title: Exceptional
resultRanges.description: Outstanding logical reasoning abilities. You demonstrate superior pattern recognition and deductive thinking skills, consistently identifying valid conclusions and complex sequence rules.
recommendations: Pursue advanced study in formal logic, discrete mathematics, or algorithmic problem solving
Apply your reasoning strengths to real-world analytical or strategic decision-making roles

questions.questionText: Study the pattern sequence. Which shape comes next? The sequence repeats circle → square → triangle with colors blue → red → green in that cycle. [SVG: public/images/patterns/pattern-1.svg in source repo]
Identify the next shape in the sequence. The number of sides increases by 1 each time: shapes shown have 3, 4, 5, and 6 sides in sequence. [SVG: public/images/patterns/pattern-2.svg in source repo]
The arrow rotates 90° clockwise each step, completing a full circle over 4 steps. Which direction comes next? [SVG: public/images/patterns/pattern-3.svg in source repo]
Observe the pattern where quantities double: dot groups shown as 1, 2, 4, 8 in sequence. What comes next? [SVG: public/images/patterns/pattern-4.svg in source repo]
Shapes alternate between filled and outlined while increasing in size (circles shown small→large, filled/outline alternating). What's next? [SVG: public/images/patterns/pattern-5.svg in source repo]
Colors progress through the spectrum: red, orange, yellow, green, blue shown in sequence. Which color comes next? [SVG: public/images/patterns/pattern-6.svg in source repo]

options.label: Maria might have studied hard, or she might be naturally talented
